pull.title: test: speed up wallet unit test
pull.body:
Deduplicates wallet creation code and avoid pre-deriving a large keypool (default 1000) by setting wallet keypool_size = 1

Speedup:

| Suite | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| coinselector_tests | 8.26 s | 3.35 s |
| wallet_tests | 2.10 s | 1.68 s |
| spend_tests | 0.59 s | 0.18 s |
| group_outputs_tests | 0.33 s | 0.12 s |

| `spend_tests`         |         0.74 (0.74–0.75) |     0.24 (0.24–0.24) |            68% |
| `group_outputs_tests` |         0.38 (0.38–0.38) |     0.13 (0.13–0.13) |            66% |

events.body: Thanks for the reviews! Force-pushed 5b70468637e00349ec9a7be35c84995f405a91e0 addressing @davidgumberg comments. I also dropped the `cchain` param of  `CreateSyncedWallet` to simplify it since all callers just passed the active chain.

tACK 5b70468637

Retested on macOS 27.2.1 arm64 against master `9183edd25e`. The update addresses davidgumberg's nits; the keypool remains at 1.

All 18 wallet unit test suites (83 test cases) pass on both revisions. The performance improvement remains: median time for `coinselector_tests` was 10.16 s on master versus 3.88 s with this PR.

comments.body:
concept ack. this follows the functional tests:

```
test/functional/test_framework/util.py:        f.write("keypool=1\n")
nit: Since the only "users" of `wallet_name` here and below set dummy values, maybe the name parameter can be dropped from `NewWallet()`?

In https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36832/changes/4ebe3d9597fa090438f95d33801428894ba69c9b (_test: deduplicate wallet creation into NewWallet helper_)

nanonit: If retouching this commit message should probably include `refactor:`

Observation/question: Why were tests using `CreateSyncedWallet()` passing before this change?

Also, if you avoid refactoring this line, I think the interface for `NewWallet` is a little better taking the node argument since then you don't need to do the member access and pointer dereference at every call site, the same could apply to `CreateSyncedWallet()` whose callers are all also doing the same thing.

> Why were tests using `CreateSyncedWallet()` passing before this change?

I'm not sure what you mean. It didn't change any behaviour because `CreateSyncedWallet()` used to create a wallet just like `NewWallet()` but now it reuses the `NewWallet()` to deduplicate code.

> I think the interface for NewWallet is a little better taking the node argument

At first I thought passing chain makes more sense for a wallet function but with your comment I realized it doesn't matter much and the benefits of passing node context directly are better. Done on 5b70468637e00349ec9a7be35c84995f405a91e0.

Right, but `NewWallet()` does more initialization stuff than just creating the `CWallet` object, it just seemed like a smell to me that those tests should pass without the wallet having the descriptor flag, and without SPKM's set up, but it's probably fine, I have not looked close.
